messages:
Samira (People Ops): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A thread — opening this for any leftover questions about reviews, comp, and appeal logistics. Drop them here and we'll reply.
Alex (Eng): Thanks! First Q: when will managers get the standard feedback template so we can share with teams?
Maya (People Ops): Well publish the feedback template and manager notes by 2026-10-03. Short version: 3 strengths, 2 areas to grow, 3 examples of impact.
Tina: If someone is on parental leave during the window, how does that affect evaluation?
Samira (People Ops): Good Q. Time off doesn't penalize performance. Managers should document the review period they evaluated and attach context. We also offer deferred review routing — DM if you need it.
Marco: On compensation: is there a cap for promotion-related salary increases this cycle?
Maya (People Ops): No hard cap company-wide; org budgets apply. Typical promotion increases average 8-18% depending on level. Managers will get guidance during calibration.
Alex (Eng): Can employees request anonymized breakdowns of promotions by gender/region?
Samira (People Ops): We'll publish org-level aggregates (no names) after calibration: counts by level and basic demographics where available to check for fairness.
Tina: Appeal timeline question  if someone files an appeal, how long until resolution?
Maya (People Ops): Standard SLA: 21 calendar days from appeal receipt. We prioritize faster for serious cases.
HR Bot: Reminder: Promotion form live 2026-10-05 at https://redwood.internal/promote.
Marco: One practical thing  any checklist for managers when writing their calibration notes?
Maya (People Ops): Yes  short checklist: 1) clear impact statement, 2) 3 artifacts (links), 3) answer the question "what changed if they were promoted?", 4) recommended comp band. We'll post the doc.
Samira (People Ops): Thanks everyone  we'll pin the templates here. If your manager needs help collecting artifacts, ask People Ops for a prep session. :slightly_smiling_face:
